utterances.text: And in that period, did the Serbs ever attack any area outside that?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK BARRIOT
utterances.text: No. This is a very important point. When we talk about the war in Croatia which lasted from 1991 to 1995, which ended by and large by the Storm operation which I witnessed this war, which lasted five years, these Serbs fought for six months only, in other words, in the second half of 1991, whereas they had been attacked for the last five years by the Croatian forces. I think that's the first important point. The second point is that the Serbs fought in the second half of 1991 for six months. They didn't fight in Zagreb or Rijeka or in Croatia. They fought in Krajina only. They fought on their own ground, and they fought in that region where they had been made martyrs in World War II. The Ustashas of Ante Pavelic and an independent Croatia. So it's easy to understand when the Serbs saw all these symbols of the Ustasha emerging in those regions where they had been massacred in World War II, where there was a genocide, they of course defended themselves. This was a legitimate self-defence situation. They were defending their own territory. And this happened -- this did not occur anywhere else in Croatia. It's very important to stress this point. And the military of UNPROFOR did time and time again emphasise this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Barriot. Please tell me something about Krajina and Bosnia now in 1994 and 1995, as briefly as possible, about Operation Storm against Western Slavonia and Operation Flash against Krajina. You were there, so what can you say about Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK BARRIOT
utterances.text: So as far as 1994 and 1995 are concerned, in 1994 I was a Blue Helmet in Krajina. The fighting took place in the Bihac pocket essentially, which is very nearby between the 5th Corps of the Bosnian army and the Muslims, moderate Muslims who had been -- remained loyal to Fikret Abdic. I was in contact with a close friend of Fikret Abdic at the time. As far as 1995 is concerned, it is true to say that the fighting took place primarily on two occasions. These were two additional attacks launched by the Croatian forces against the UN protected areas I talked about, the three attacks in 1992 and 1993. In 1995 there were two additional attacks. The first one took place at the beginning of May 1995, which is the Flash operation, Operation Flash, where the Croatian forces were supported by the US army and attacked Slavonia, and Western Slavonia. They attacked Pakrac, Okucani and Jasenovac and there was a deluge of fire on this region. Something like 5.000 refugees fled the area in the direction of Stari Gradiska harbour where the MiG 21, which were Croatians, started shelling them. They moved in direction of Banja Luka. Then let me repeat: On this occasion several hundred Serbs died. Milan Martic had asked me to appeal to the French press agency Agence France Presse, which is what I did, but these appeals were not broadcast by the French press agency. So much for the Flash operation. As far as the Operation Storm is concerned, let me repeat I witnessed these events with my own eyes. This started at the beginning of August 1995. I'd like to emphasise that this started with US strikes against the -- the Serb position, and the US army was directly involved in this particular instance. The -- the Operation Storm was terrible and caused the deaths of more than a thousand Serbs and caused the largest exodus ever in the former Yugoslavia. Two hundred thousand Serbs had to flee Krajina. And I stress this, that this was a well-accomplished ethnic cleansing operation, because the Serbs never returned to their homes after that. So these were massive massacres, destruction on a large scale of all the farms, expulsion of some 200.000 Serbs, whereas the Krajina was entirely disarmed. I would like to stress an important point here. At the beginning of May, I was in Knin. I met General Loncar, the Serb general, who told me, "I thank you to be on the side of the losers," and the Serbs in Krajina in May, at the time of Operation Flash against Western Slavonia, knew that their turn would come and knew that they would be unable to defend themselves because they were not armed and were confronted with a very powerful army which had been supported and armed by the US [Realtime transcript read in error "Croatian"] and the international community so that it didn't stand a chance. When I said they had been disarmed this was confirmed afterwards. When the Croatian troops arrived in Krajina, they discovered a few tanks that had run out of petrol, a few rocket launchers here and there, but no heavy weaponry and no means and ways of defending themselves against the Croatian army, particularly as it had been so well equipped by the US army and military profession -- Military Professional Resources Incorporated, a private company.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: May I clarify one thing? It's because of something that didn't appear in the transcript although it seemed to be said. Did you say that in relation to Operation Flash that the Croatian army were supported by the army of the United States?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. The transcript says that it is supported by the Croatian army but it should be corrected. And if you could clarify the meaning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I talked about Operation Flash against Western Slavonia. In May of 1995, and I said that the Croatian army had been equipped by the US, by the private company MPRI, and as far as the operation, Storm operation in August 1995 against Krajina, I stipulated that the Croatian forces had been equipped by the US. I also emphasised that the US army intervened directly outside the framework of NATO by attacking the Serb positions in Knin to enable the Croatian forces to move in freely. I'd like to say that military from the Military Professional Resource Incorporated company intervened directly on the territory of the Krajina. Of Canadian officers, UN Canadian officers stated this quite clearly. They stated having seen these American military in Knin in August of 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Milosevic, we have to break now. We're going to break --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just -- I understand that we have to break now and that our time is up, but let me just try to understand something. I'm listening to the Serbian interpretation. I don't know what the witness said, or in this transcript, rather, 49.18 it says "outside the framework of NATO." Did the witness say that, outside NATO or outside the United Nations? The interpretation I received was that they intervened without approval of the United Nations. So now I don't know what the witness actually said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you could indicate the number of lines and page and line number. The clock differs.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have it on the transcript right in front of us now. 14.13 -- no. No. It changes all the time. 14.13.49.18. The interpretation I received was the UN.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let me read what is on the transcript to the witness. It says here, Mr. Barriot: "I also emphasised that the US army intervened directly outside the framework of NATO by attacking the Serb positions in Knin, et cetera." Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I wanted to emphasise that this was a deliberate initiative by the United States outside --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Outside the framework of NATO, that's what you said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] United Nations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: United Nations. Then that's corrected. We'll take the break now and resume tomorrow morning at 9.00 a.m.
